title: DIAMETER: Do not use IP/Port for conversation
description:
Conversation search will failed in cases of multi-homed SCTP or multiple TCP (loadshare more) connections
as Requests and Responses may come from different IP/Port.

Add option to disable such behaviour and use only End-To-End and
Hop-By-Hop.

Trace example [diam_sctp_multihome.pcap](/uploads/d2881a94c440e93a862496607f15a4c4/diam_sctp_multihome.pcap)

- Packet 1 and 2 - source IP and destination IP are matched => Coversation found.
- Packet 3 and 4 - source IP and destination IP are matched but Hop-By-Hop is different => Conversation not found
- Packet 5 and 6 - source IP and destination IP are not matched => Conversation found only in case if option disabled [This is our case]
- Packet 7 and 8 - source IP and destination IP are not matched but Hop-By-Hop is different -> Conversation not found

notes.body:
This creates an large amount of unnecessary memory overhead, because everything is already stored in a multimap keyed by the hop by hop id.

Rather than create a separate conversation and conversation data struct for each pair of IDs (and thus a lot of trees with exactly one node), you would achieve the same results with less wasted memory by not using a conversation at all and simply having a single structure containing all the request and replies.

  • 96224f43...3ad01955 - 196 commits from branch wireshark:master
  • 034bcb95 - DIAMETER: Do not use IP/Port for conversation
[Compare with previous version](/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/19625/diffs?diff_id=1358194400&start_sha=96224f43c9cfcb0b74cebd44da476e3dc4b5d327)

Hmm, I understand why you want to do this. However, if you are not matching by the underlying conversation (side note: there's an argument that SCTP should deal with multi-homing if possible, as it has some ability to track associations, though the capture file you attached doesn't have enough of the other SCTP chunks to determine that), that does increase the chance of a collision of the Hop-to-Hop ID.

Right now, if the Hop-to-Hop ID collides (which now can occur with interleaved transactions with different senders using the same Hop-to-Hop ID), then matching won't work. It might eventually make sense to change the tree to a multimap.
Can you share example (pcap file or some detailes of SCTP chunks and Hope-By-Hope and End-to-End IDs) of such scenario?

It's a low probability scenario, but there is a chance of a collision, unlike when using the network layer information. RFC 6733 says that "The sender MUST ensure that the Hop-by-Hop Identifier in a request is unique on a given connection at any given time", where connection is defined in the RFC 6733 sense and can include dealing with multihoming, but there is clearly no such guarantee when not making any attempt to divide by connections. Two different connections could choose to use the same Hop-by-Hop ID.

#18210 is a similar example of a collision in SMB3 after commit 46d6230cd463334e1039b0d7c4752b5f413a688b, which dealt with SMB2 multichannel in what is fairly similar to the situation here.

I don't think it really makes sense to add all the conversation API stuff and add something to conversation.h when you only have one conversation for the entire protocol. Why not just have a static `diameter_pdu_trees` at file scope, similar to the change mentioned above?

Changing the tree to lookup via both the hop-by-hop id and the end-to-end id by using `wmem_tree_lookup32_array` would handle the vast majority of collisions and should be sufficient. By doing that, I think that the chance of collision would be rare enough that there wouldn't be a need to have a preference; we could just always use the hop-by-hop id and end-to-end id alone and not use the network layer.
I prefer keep preference to enable/disable matching by IP/Port

Or the tree lookup that is currently just by hop-by-hop could be changed to an array that uses both the hop-by-hop ID and the end-to-end ID.

I suppose in the short run you could go back to adding the end-to-end ID (but not the hop-by-hop ID, as it's redundant) to the conversation key.
